Grace Fellowship is a non-denominational community on Austin's east side, focused on simple, welcoming worship and hands-on local outreach. Services run every Sunday with programming for kids and youth during the main service.

Founded in 2009, the church has grown into a close-knit congregation of around 300 regular attendees, with small groups meeting throughout the week across the city.

Help

Frequently asked questions

How do I find a church near me?

Use the search bar on the homepage, or go to Churches to browse and filter by denomination, distance, or keyword.

How do I follow a church or set a Church Home?

Visit any church's page — you'll find a "Follow church" button, and on the Location tab, a "Make this my Church Home" button. Both require a free account.

How do I register my church as an administrator?

Sign up like anyone else — there's no separate choice to make. Then register your church from the Pricing page or the "Add a church" button on your Profile or My Churches page — your account automatically becomes a church administrator account, and you're taken straight to your church dashboard once it's created.

How does online giving work?

Church owners connect a bank account through Stripe in their dashboard's Giving section. New churches need to be verified first — request verification from that same section, and donations go directly to the church's own account; FaithDock never holds the funds.

How do I join a group?

On a church's page, go to the Groups tab and click into any group to see how to join — some are open to anyone, others require a request or an invite from the group's leader.

I'm a church administrator — how do I add staff?

In your dashboard's Team panel (under Settings), enter a staff member's email to add them. You can also control exactly what each staff member is allowed to manage — events, giving, billing, or the church profile — individually.

How do I switch the site to Spanish?

Click the "EN / ES" button in the top navigation, on any page. Your choice is remembered on your next visit.

How do I delete my account?

Go to your Profile page and scroll to "Delete account." If you own a church, you'll need to delete the church first from your dashboard's Settings before your account can be deleted.

Still need help?

Send a message and our team will get back to you.

Giving

Connect a bank account so your church can accept donations directly through FaithDock. Donations go straight to your account — FaithDock never holds the funds.

Facility rooms

The spaces your church schedules — classrooms, the sanctuary, Rec Center, outdoor areas. These show up as options when creating an event.

Transfer ownership

Hand this church off to someone else. Nothing changes until they explicitly accept — this doesn't transfer instantly just because you send it, and you can cancel it anytime before they respond.

Giving funds

Designated funds donors can choose from when giving — a building campaign, a mission trip, whatever your church tracks separately. Gifts with no fund selected count toward the General Fund.

Team

Staff can create and edit events. Church profile and billing stay owner-only.

If they already have a FaithDock account, they're added right away. If not, they'll get an email invite and join automatically once they sign up.

Privacy Policy

Last updated: September 2026

FaithDock LLC ("FaithDock," "we," "us") operates faithdock.com, a platform that helps people find churches and events, and helps churches manage their community, events, groups, and giving. This page explains what information we collect, why, and how you can control it.

What we collect

When you create an account, we collect your name and email address, and — if you sign in with Google — the basic profile information Google shares with us (name, email, profile photo). You can also optionally add a phone number, a profile photo, and a general age range; age range is used only for anonymous, aggregated reporting a church might see (like "giving by age group") and is never shown next to your name or shared individually.

If you follow or join a church, we store that relationship, along with any household relationships (like spouse or child) you choose to add. If you register for an event, join a group, or check in at a church, we store that activity so the church can see its own attendance and involvement. If you give financially through FaithDock, payment processing is handled entirely by Stripe — FaithDock never holds or has direct access to your card details, and donations go straight to the receiving church's own account.

We do not collect background-check information, detailed health records, or emergency-contact information for children, and we do not knowingly collect information from children under 13.

How we use it

We use your information to run the core features of FaithDock: showing you churches and events near you, letting you register and follow along, and giving churches the tools to manage their own community. We send account-related emails (like confirming your signup, or notifying you of account changes) through Resend, our email provider. If something goes wrong in your browser, a basic error report (what happened, and which page) may be sent to us automatically to help us fix it — this never includes your password or payment details.

Who we share it with

We don't sell your personal information, and we don't share it with advertisers. A church you follow, join, or register for an event with can see the information relevant to that relationship (like your name, contact info, and attendance) — the same way it would if you walked into that church in person. We use a small number of service providers to actually run FaithDock: Supabase (our database and login system), Stripe (payment processing for giving), Resend (sending emails), Google (optional sign-in, and location search for maps), and Cloudflare (basic bot protection on our forms). Each only receives the information it needs to do its specific job.

Your choices

You can review and update most of your information any time from your Profile page, including your name, phone number, age range, and email. You can delete your account entirely from your Profile page as well — this removes your personal data, though records a church needs to keep for its own legitimate purposes (like a giving record for tax purposes) may be retained by that church separately, the same way a paper receipt would be.

Contact us

If you have questions about this policy or your data, reach us at team@faithdock.com.

FaithDock is currently in early testing ahead of a wider launch. This policy will be reviewed and updated as the product grows.

Legal

Terms of Service

Last updated: September 2026

These terms govern your use of FaithDock, operated by FaithDock LLC. By creating an account or using the site, you agree to them.

Using FaithDock

You need to provide accurate information when you sign up, and you're responsible for keeping your login secure. You must be at least 13 years old to create an account. If you're setting up or managing a church's presence on FaithDock, you're responsible for the accuracy of what you post about that church, and for how your church's staff use the access you give them.

Content and conduct

Don't post anything illegal, harassing, or deliberately false, and don't use FaithDock to send spam or unsolicited mass messages outside its intended use. We may remove content or suspend accounts that violate these terms.

Giving and payments

Donations made through FaithDock are processed by Stripe and go directly to the receiving church's own connected account — FaithDock is not a party to that transaction and does not hold or refund funds on a church's behalf. Any dispute about a specific donation is between the giver and the receiving church.

No warranty

FaithDock is currently an early-stage product, provided as-is, without warranty of any kind. We work to keep it accurate and available, but we can't guarantee it will always be error-free or uninterrupted.

Changes

We may update these terms as FaithDock grows. We'll post the updated version here with a new date.

Contact us

Questions about these terms can be sent to team@faithdock.com.

Legal

Accessibility Statement

Last updated: September 2026

FaithDock is committed to making our site usable by everyone, including people who use assistive technology like screen readers, screen magnifiers, or keyboard-only navigation. This statement describes where we stand today and how to reach us if something isn't working for you.

Our standard

We're working toward conformance with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA — the widely used standard for web accessibility, also referenced by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). This includes things like sufficient color contrast, keyboard-operable navigation and forms, descriptive labels for interactive elements, and alt text for meaningful images.

Where we are today

FaithDock is currently an early-stage prototype, not a finished product (see our Terms of Service). Accessibility work is ongoing alongside everything else we're building, so some areas — particularly newer or more complex features — may not yet fully meet this standard. We treat accessibility issues as real bugs, not polish, and prioritize fixing them when they're reported.

Tell us what isn't working

If you use assistive technology and run into something on FaithDock that doesn't work the way it should, we want to know. Please tell us the page you were on, what you were trying to do, and what happened instead — that's the fastest way for us to reproduce and fix it.

Contact us

Reach us about accessibility at team@faithdock.com.
